error_chain: axum's Router stores routes in a path_router and applies layer() globally to the underlying service stack
route_layer() in axum's Router differs: it wraps only routes currently registered, not routes added later via merge
tower's ServiceBuilder composes layers in declaration order; the wrapped Service is built from the inner-most layer outward

When the customer calls Router::merge(sub_router) after Router::route_layer(auth), axum's path_router merges sub_router's routes into the parent without re-applying route_layer, leaving those endpoints unwrapped by the auth layer
trigger_conditions: Customer's code uses Router::route_layer(auth_layer) followed by Router::merge(sub_router) to attach modular routes
axum's route_layer applies only to routes registered before the merge call; merged routes bypass it
tower's ServiceBuilder is unaware of axum's per-route routing decisions, so the Layer is effectively absent for the merged subset

expected_answer.error_origin: axum's Router::route_layer does not wrap routes added later via Router::merge; tower's ServiceBuilder layer is never composed for those routes
expected_answer.bypass_reason: route_layer() only applies to routes already in the Router; merge() adds new routes outside that wrap
expected_answer.correct_config: Use Router::layer (global) instead of route_layer for auth, or apply route_layer AFTER all merges, or use middleware::from_fn on the merged sub-router so the layer travels with its routes
